LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Melody. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs
2. use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MELODY
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Melody helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MELODY
Study Melody like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy

What this means
In this part you learn to use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Melody is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words. (skill: use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Melody to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs.
3. Practise this skill: use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Melody from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Melody: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Melody?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Melody means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate own and others • Learners use digital devices to record and compositions, playback their own variations to familiar songs.
5. Be able to: use digital devices to record own variations to familiar songs for enjoyment and digital literacy.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
